questions.q: Which tag gives the largest heading on a web page?
questions.explain: <h1> is the largest heading (the main title) and <h6> is the smallest. <head> holds metadata, and <title> shows in the browser tab.

questions.q: A learner wants a bulleted list with square bullets. Which opening tag must they use?
questions.explain: A bulleted list is an unordered list, <ul>. Its type can be square, circle or disc. <ol> is a numbered (ordered) list, and <li> is one list item.

questions.q: In the CSS rule h1 { color: blue; }, what is h1?
questions.explain: A rule set is a selector plus a declaration. h1 is the selector; color: blue; is the declaration, where color is the property and blue is the value.

questions.q: What colour is the hexadecimal colour #00FF00?
questions.explain: Hexadecimal colours are #RRGGBB, with FF = 255 and 00 = 0. #00FF00 is no red, full green and no blue, the same as rgb(0, 255, 0).

questions.q: Cells A1 to A5 hold: Apple, 10, 20, (empty), 30. What does =AVERAGE(A1:A5) give?
questions.explain: AVERAGE ignores text and blanks, so it works with 10, 20 and 30 only: (10 + 20 + 30) ÷ 3 = 60 ÷ 3 = 20.

questions.q: What is the next number in the pattern 1, 2, 4, 7, 11, …?
questions.explain: The differences are +1, +2, +3, +4, so they grow by 1 each time. The next difference is +5, and 11 + 5 = 16.

questions.q: Which line correctly stores a learner's height of 1.65 m in Java?
questions.explain: 1.65 is a decimal, so it needs a double. An int stores whole numbers only, a boolean stores only true or false, and a String needs text in double quotes.

questions.q: Which of these is a valid Java variable name?
questions.explain: A name may not start with a number (1stPlayer), may not contain spaces (player score) and may not be a reserved word (public). The underscore is the only special character allowed, so player_1 is valid.

questions.q: What is an embedded system?
options: A computer that can run almost any software
A specialised computer built for one specific, dedicated job
The brain of a general-purpose computer
A program that runs inside a web page
questions.explain: An embedded system does one dedicated job, like a router, a microwave controller or a car engine controller. A general-purpose computer can run almost any software.

sections.title: True or false
sections.intro: Decide whether each statement is true or false.

questions.q: HTML is a programming language.
questions.explain: HTML is a markup language that tells a browser how to display content. It is not a programming language.

questions.q: The alt text of an image is shown if the image fails to load.
questions.explain: alt is the alternative text for blind users, and it shows when the image cannot load, for example when the picture is not in the same folder as the HTML file.

questions.q: Inline CSS is the preferred way to style a website.
questions.explain: Inline CSS is the worst way: you have to style each line separately. External CSS (a separate .css file) is preferred, because one file can style 50+ pages.

questions.q: If you delete a worksheet by mistake, you can undo it.
questions.explain: Deleting a sheet cannot be undone, so check before you delete.

questions.q: In jGRASP, a syntax error stops the compiler, so no .class file is created.
questions.explain: The compiler only saves the bytecode as a .class file once the code has no syntax errors. Fix the error first, then compile again.

questions.q: Construction lines in FreeCAD become part of the final 3D model.
questions.explain: Construction lines are blue guide lines used to plan and measure. They are never part of the final 3D model.

questions.q: A voltmeter is connected in parallel and an ammeter in series.
questions.explain: A voltmeter measures voltage across a component, so it goes in parallel. An ammeter measures the current flowing through, so it goes in series.

sections.title: Matching
sections.intro: Match column A to column B, and find the matching pairs.

questions.q: Match each feature of the Arduino Uno in column A with its specification in column B.
questions.explain: 7 to 12 V is the recommended input voltage through the barrel jack, not the operating voltage. Flash memory is non-volatile, so the program stays when the power is off; the 2 KB of SRAM holds variables only while the program runs.

questions.q: Find the matching pairs: link each pillar of computational thinking to an example of it.
pairs: Splitting the job of building a robot into parts, bolts and steps
Netflix suggesting shows like the ones you watched
A map that shows only roads and landmarks
Precise step-by-step instructions for a robot to make a sandwich
questions.explain: Decomposition breaks a big problem into smaller parts. Pattern recognition spots repeats and trends to predict. Abstraction leaves out unnecessary detail. An algorithm is a clear, precise set of steps, because a robot has no intuition.

questions.q: Match each FreeCAD term in column A with its meaning in column B.
pairs: The main container that holds all the 3D features of one part
A flat 2D drawing on a chosen plane
A rounded edge added to a sharp corner
A reference surface you create to sketch from a new angle or position
extra: The point where the X, Y and Z axes meet
questions.explain: The extra description in column B is the Origin. A sketch is the starting point for a 3D shape, and a fillet makes a model smoother, safer and stronger.

sections.title: Steps in order
sections.intro: Put the steps in the correct order.

questions.q: Put the steps for inserting a chart in Excel in the correct order.
steps: Highlight them (hold Ctrl for columns that are not next to each other)
Select the chart type, e.g. 2D column or pie
questions.explain: Decide, highlight, Insert tab, chart type. Afterwards the Chart Design tab changes the colours, style, layout or chart type.

questions.q: Put the steps for making a 3D part in FreeCAD in the correct order.
steps: Create a sketch on the XY plane
Draw the outline and add constraints until the sketch turns green
Pad the sketch into a 3D part
questions.explain: Every part starts with Create Body → Create Sketch → choose a plane. Fully constrain the sketch (green, zero DOF) before you Pad it, then save. The first save is Save As.

sections.title: Scenarios
sections.intro: Read each scenario, then answer the questions about it.

questions.scenario: Sipho makes a page for the school's robotics club. This is his code:
questions.code:
Robotics Club

Meetings on Fridays

questions.q: Where will the words Robotics Club from the <title> tag appear?
options: As the biggest heading on the page
In the title bar or browser tab
Nowhere, because it is a comment
questions.explain: The <title> sits in the <head>, which is not displayed on the page. The title shows in the title bar or browser tab. The big heading on the page comes from <h1>.

questions.q: The page shows the words Our robot instead of the picture. What is the most likely reason?
options: The width and height are too big
robot.png is not in the same folder as the HTML file
The <a> tag is missing a closing tag
questions.explain: Keep pictures in the same folder as the HTML file, otherwise the image will not show and the alt text appears instead.

questions.q: What happens when a visitor clicks the picture?
options: Nothing, because pictures cannot be links
Wikipedia opens in a new tab
questions.explain: The is wrapped inside an tag, so the picture is a link. target="_blank" opens it in a new tab, which keeps visitors on Sipho's site.

questions.q: Sipho may use class="red-text" on several other paragraphs on the same page.
questions.explain: A class is reusable and can be used many times. An id is the one that must be unique, used once per page.

questions.scenario: Zanele writes this code for her Gogga, ziggy.

questions.q: How many times does ziggy.move() run?
questions.explain: counter starts at 0 and the loop runs while counter < 6, so it runs for 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5: 6 times.

questions.q: In the for loop, which part is counter++?
questions.explain: A for loop has three parts: initialisation (int counter = 0), condition (counter < 6) and increment (counter++, short for counter = counter + 1).

questions.q: Why is counter declared as an int?
questions.explain: counter counts 0, 1, 2, …, which are whole numbers, so int is the right data type.

questions.q: ziggy.turnRight() runs 6 times, once after every move.
questions.explain: ziggy.turnRight() comes after the closing } of the loop, so it is not repeated: it runs once, after all 6 moves.

questions.scenario: Ayanda builds the Blinky LED circuit in TinkerCAD, but she powers it from a 9 V battery instead of an Arduino pin. The LED drops about 2 V, and she wants a current of 10 mA (0.01 A).

questions.q: What voltage must the resistor take?
questions.explain: The battery gives 9 V and the LED drops 2 V, so the resistor takes 9 − 2 = 7 V.

questions.q: Which resistor does she need?
questions.explain: R = V ÷ I = 7 ÷ 0.01 = 700 Ω. (350 Ω would be the answer for 20 mA.)

questions.q: Why does the LED need a resistor at all?
options: The LED has very low internal resistance, so on its own it draws too much current and burns out
questions.explain: An LED has very low internal resistance. Connected directly, it draws too much current and burns out. A current-limiting resistor in series protects it.

questions.q: In the Blinky program, setting the LED pin HIGH switches the LED off.
questions.explain: HIGH is 5 V, which switches the LED on. LOW (0 V) switches it off. Blinky: HIGH → wait 1 second → LOW → wait 1 second.
